name: PdxSortableList
description:
A list the user can put in another order, by dragging a row's handle or from the keyboard alone.

It emits `pdx-reorder` with the indices and never writes to `items`: the application applies the
move, so the array it owns stays the one source of truth.

members.name: idField
members.description: How a row is identified. Empty: the row's index.

members.name: labelField
members.description: What a row shows without an `item` slot, and what names its handle either way.

members.name: handle
members.description: A selector inside the row that the POINTER may grab. Empty: the rendered handle.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

events.name: pdx-reorder
events.description: A row was dropped at another position: `from` and `to` are indices into `items`, `id` the row's `id-field`. The list is not changed: the application moves the item.
events.detail: { from: number; to: number; id: unknown }

attributes.name: idfield
attributes.description: How a row is identified. Empty: the row's index.

attributes.name: labelfield
attributes.description: What a row shows without an `item` slot, and what names its handle either way.

attributes.name: handle
attributes.description: A selector inside the row that the POINTER may grab. Empty: the rendered handle.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

slots.name: item
slots.description:
Renders one row's content: a snippet `item(item, index)`. Without it the row shows
the item's `label-field`.

cssParts.name: item
cssParts.description: A row, `<li>`. The row lifted from the keyboard carries `pdx-sortable-item-lifted`.

cssParts.name: handle
cssParts.description: A row's handle, the button the pointer grabs and the keyboard moves.

cssStates.name: disabled
cssStates.description: `disabled` is set: nothing can be moved, and the handles are `aria-disabled`.
